# Disconnected tangential logarithmic defects from actual convex profile cuts

This gives an exact geometric obstruction to treating the linked zero-face defect as the uniform law, a concave density, or even an absolutely continuous measure on a lower-dimensional face. It uses actual changing convex bodies, positive finite-plane concave parameters, and exact volume contact rows with uniformly interior source marks. The defect can have disconnected tangential support inside one exposed zero face. A one-affine-plane example in Section 6 produces a genuine atom at a relative-interior point of that face; Section 7 realizes every prescribed finite atomic tangential measure.

The construction does **not** assert that its source marks are deepest or that it carries the ordinary physical cap-stress certificate. Thus it isolates a genuine failure of a geometric classification based only on finite-plane parameters, convex bodies, and their actual volume rows. Any stronger theorem using deepestness or the cap-load inequality must use that additional information.

## 1. A realizable profile class

Let F be a full-dimensional compact convex polytope in R^m, m>=1. Let A,H be positive convex finite-PL functions on F, with A>=H. Put d=m+2, use coordinates (s,x,y), and set t=x+y. For integers j large enough define

    delta_j=1/j,  eta_j=exp(-j),
    K_j={(s,x,y):s in F, x,y>=0,
                         delta_j A(s)<=x+y<=1},
    ell_j(s,x,y)=x+y-delta_j H(s)+eta_j,
    c_j=exp[-|K_j|^(-1) integral_(K_j) log ell_j],
    L_j=c_j ell_j.                                    (1)

The bodies are convex: the lower bound is the epigraph of the convex function delta_j A, and every other constraint is convex. Their parameters are positive and concave finite-PL, with minimum at least c_j eta_j. Indeed the raw parameter is the minimum of the finitely many affine functions t-delta_j H_r(s)+eta_j, where H=max_r H_r. They are therefore positive on a neighborhood of each current compact body. Each (1) is an actual n=0 convex family; taking its product with any fixed complete base gives compatible equal fibers as well.

The bodies converge in Hausdorff distance to

    K=F times {(x,y):x,y>=0,x+y<=1}.

Their masses converge to M=|F|/2. The raw parameters converge uniformly on a common box to t. Furthermore

    c_j -> c=exp(1/2),   L_j -> L=c(x+y)              (2)

uniformly as finite-plane functions. To check the normalization, use x=t r,y=t(1-r), 0<=r<=1, with volume element t dt dr ds. At each s put b=delta_j H(s)-eta_j. An antiderivative of t log(t-b) is

    G_b(v)=v^2 log v/2-v^2/4+b(v log v-v), v=t-b.

The upper endpoint tends uniformly to -1/4. The lower endpoint is v=delta_j(A-H)+eta_j; its absolute value tends uniformly to zero, since v=O(delta_j), b=O(delta_j), and v log v and v^2 log v vanish at zero. Thus integral log ell_j tends to -|F|/4, proving (2).

## 2. Exact inverse-volume defect

At each s, the integral over the normal triangle is

    Z_j(s)=integral_(delta_j A(s))^1 t/[t-delta_j H(s)+eta_j] dt
       =1-delta_j A(s)
          +(delta_j H(s)-eta_j)
             log[(1-delta_j H(s)+eta_j)
                         /(delta_j(A(s)-H(s))+eta_j)].  (3)

Let E={s in F:A(s)=H(s)}. If s belongs to E, the last term tends to H(s). If A(s)>H(s), it tends to zero. The logarithm is nonnegative and bounded above by j plus a uniform constant, while delta_j H is uniformly O(1/j). Hence (3) is uniformly bounded and dominated convergence applies in s.

More precisely, write t/(t-b)=1+b/(t-b). The first term in this decomposition tends to the ordinary density dm/t. For every fixed r_0>0, the second term restricted to t>=r_0 has mass O(delta_j) uniformly in s. Its remaining mass therefore concentrates at (x,y)=(0,0), and uniform continuity of a test function identifies the full weak limit:

    dm_j/ell_j -> dm/(x+y)
                  +H(s)1_E(s) ds delta_((x,y)=(0,0)). (4)

After actual mixed-volume and logarithmic normalization, the inverse defect is

    zeta=[2/(|F|c)] H(s)1_E(s) ds delta_((x,y)=(0,0)). (5)

The limiting parameter vanishes on the single exposed face F times {(0,0)}. Its inverse is integrable in K; the defect in (5) is additional to that ordinary inverse density.

## 3. Exact surface-log defect

On the lower surface, the parametrization

    (s,r) -> (s,delta_j A(s)r,delta_j A(s)(1-r))

has area element

    delta_j A(s) sqrt[2+delta_j^2 |grad A(s)|^2] ds dr,

and outward normal

    n_j(s)=[delta_j grad A(s),-1,-1]
                        /sqrt[2+delta_j^2 |grad A(s)|^2].

These formulas hold a.e.; the finitely many PL seams have zero surface measure. The parameter on this surface is c_j[delta_j(A-H)+eta_j]. Thus its negative-log weighted area tends, pointwise and in total mass, to

    sqrt(2) A(s)1_E(s) ds dr.

The domination follows directly from -log[delta_j(A-H)+eta_j]<=j and bounded A,grad A,c_j. On E, A=H, so the exact boundary defect on the normal bundle is

    b=sqrt(2) H(s)1_E(s) ds
          delta_((x,y)=(0,0)) delta_(n_0),
    n_0=(0,...,0,-1,-1)/sqrt(2).                      (6)

There are no other defect contributions. On the sides x=0 or y=0, integrate log(t-delta_j H+eta_j) in dt. The primitive v log v-v makes the lower endpoint contribution vanish uniformly, including where A=H. The logarithmic mass with t near zero is uniformly bounded by a constant times r_0(1+|log r_0|), tending to zero with r_0. On sides over boundary F the additional volume factor t only improves this bound. The upper facet has L_j>1 for all sufficiently large j. Away from t=0 all remaining boundary weights converge uniformly. These facts identify the ordinary negative-log boundary trace plus (6), without an unproved surface-density limit at the collapsing roof.

The common limiting continuous gradient is c_vec=(0,...,0,c,c). Equations (5)--(6) give pointwise in s

    -n_0 db=M c_vec d zeta.                           (7)

Thus the new tangential freedom is fully consistent with the exact flux theorem `candidate d9362f528596f345`.

## 4. These are actual contact rows with uniform source cores

Partition F, modulo null seams, into the positive-volume convex cells F_i on which a fixed affine piece H_i is active. Let D_ij be the part of K_j over F_i and let V_ij=|D_ij|. Define

    Z_ij=integral_(D_ij) 1/ell_j dm,
    d rho_ij=1_(D_ij) dm/[Z_ij ell_j],
    Y_ij=E_(rho_ij) w,
    sigma_ij=V_ij/|K_j|.

The parameter L_j is affine on the convex set D_ij. Consequently

    L_ij=L_j(Y_ij)=c_j V_ij/Z_ij,
    E_(rho_ij) L_j=L_ij,
    sum_i (sigma_ij/L_ij)rho_ij=dm_j/(|K_j| L_j),
    (L_j/L_ij)rho_ij=1_(D_ij)dm/V_ij.                 (8)

These are exact finite contact rows, not merely chosen limiting marginals. Their source planes are the corresponding affine pieces of L_j.

Every fixed F_i has positive m-volume. Formula (4), restricted to that cell, gives a limiting probability row consisting of a positive absolutely continuous component throughout F_i times the open normal triangle, and a possible boundary component on E. Its mean lies strictly inside F_i and strictly inside the normal triangle: the absolutely continuous part has full support in that convex cell, and every additional part lies in its closure. Therefore Y_ij tends to an interior point of K, and a fixed positive own-source ball lies in K_j for all sufficiently large j. Equation (3) also gives finite positive limits of Z_ij, and V_ij tends to |F_i|/2. Hence all L_ij have positive lower bounds. The number of cells is fixed, all source weights have positive limits, and the source-plane coefficients are uniformly bounded.

The original-volume rows in (8) are uniform on the actual cells and have no boundary defect. No equality of their means with the tilted means is asserted.

## 5. Two planes already give disconnected tangential support

For an explicit d=3 example let F=[0,1] and take

    H(s)=max{2-s,1+s},
    A(s)=max{2-s,17/10,1+s}.                          (9)

Then A>=H>0 and

    E=[0,3/10] union [7/10,1].                        (10)

The lower-body roof has three affine pieces, while L_j has only two. Formula (6) is positive on both intervals in (10) and zero throughout the intervening open interval. Its tangential support is disconnected, even though the limiting zero face is the entire segment [0,1] times {(0,0)}.

The two actual rows use F_-=[0,1/2] and F_+=[1/2,1]. Exact integrals are

    integral_(E intersect F_-) H=111/200,
    integral_(E intersect F_-) s H=81/1000,
    Z_-,infinity=1/2+111/200=211/200.

The ordinary inverse-density component contributes first s moment 1/8 and first x and y moments 1/8 each. Hence the limiting sources and values are

    Y_-=(206/1055,25/211,25/211),
    Y_+=(1-206/1055,25/211,25/211),
    L_-=L_+=c*50/211,  sigma_-=sigma_+=1/2.           (11)

They are strictly interior, so the uniform source-core and marked-value requirements in the linked-defect theorem hold. Equations (8) hold at every finite j, not only in the limit.

The density in (6) is neither a concave function on the zero edge nor a log-concave measure there. A nonzero log-concave measure has convex support; (10) fails that necessary condition. This also rules out interpreting this b, up to normalization, as a uniform lower-dimensional convex-body law.

More generally, any finite union E of closed subintervals of [0,1], of positive total length, can occur as the support pattern. Choose a continuous nonnegative PL function g whose zero set is E. At each breakpoint let J be the jump in its slope and choose a convex PL H with slope jump max{0,-J}; add a sufficiently large positive constant. Then A=H+g is convex PL, A>=H>0, and {A=H}=E. The preceding construction realizes its defect. This gives arbitrarily many components with a finite fixed number of planes for each sequence.

The limiting marks in (11) are not ordinary deepest: the cap x+y<=50/211 through either mark captures the fraction (50/211)^2<27/64, whereas the prism centroid has at least the ordinary dimension-three Grunbaum fraction 27/64. This gap persists for the finite bodies when j is sufficiently large. No actual physical cap-load stress is supplied. The precise conclusion is that finite-plane geometry and genuine contact rows, even with all compactness/core bounds, do not by themselves furnish a lower-dimensional convex-body or log-concave law on the zero face.

## 6. One affine plane gives an atom inside the zero edge

Tangential singularity does not require many parameter pieces. Fix p in (0,1), take delta_j=w_j=1/j, and for all sufficiently large j let

    E_j=[p-w_j,p+w_j],
    H=1,
    A_j(s)=1+dist(s,E_j),
    eta_j=exp(-j^2),
    K_j={0<=s<=1, x,y>=0:delta_j A_j(s)<=x+y<=1},
    L_j=c_j[x+y-delta_j+eta_j].                       (12)

Here A_j is convex with three affine pieces and uniformly bounded slopes. L_j is a SINGLE affine function. The bodies and parameters have the same limits as before, with M=1/2 and c_j->c=exp(1/2). The normalization follows from the same primitive; the much smaller eta_j does not change it because eta_j|log eta_j| tends to zero.

On the flat roof band E_j, the negative logarithm is j^2-log c_j, the normal is exactly n_0, and the area density is sqrt(2)delta_j. Its total logarithmic mass is

    2 w_j sqrt(2)delta_j[j^2-log c_j] ->2sqrt(2).

It concentrates at s=p. Off E_j, put r=dist(s,E_j). The logarithmic factor is bounded above by -log(delta_j r), whenever this is positive. The integral of |log r| over the two complementary intervals is uniformly bounded. Hence the entire off-band roof contribution is O(delta_j[1+|log delta_j|]) and tends to zero. The side-facet logarithms have the same uniform integrability as in Section 3. Thus

    b=2sqrt(2) delta_(n_0,p,0,0).                     (13)

Similarly, (3) on E_j has excess (delta_j-eta_j)j^2 plus a bounded negligible correction. Integration over length 2w_j gives raw inverse defect mass 2. Off E_j the preceding logarithmic estimate makes the excess O(delta_j[1+|log delta_j|]). Consequently

    dm_j/ell_j -> dm/(x+y)+2delta_(p,0,0),
    zeta=(4/c)delta_(p,0,0).                          (14)

There is one exact contact row rho_j=dm_j/[Z_j ell_j], with sigma=1 and Z_j->3. The ordinary inverse-density part has s first moment 1/2 and x and y first moments 1/4. The limiting row source is therefore

    Y=((1/2+2p)/3,1/12,1/12),
    L(Y)=c/6.                                       (15)

It is strictly interior for every p in (0,1); a fixed own-source ball and a fixed positive marked-value lower bound therefore hold along the sequence. Its original-volume row is exactly uniform on K_j. This is also a genuine fixed-MARK global parameter certificate, by the usual logarithmic contact Jensen inequality. It is not a deepest-source certificate: the cap x+y<=1/6 has limiting fraction 1/36<27/64.

The point (p,0,0) lies in the RELATIVE INTERIOR of the one-dimensional zero face, rather than in a smaller exposed face of the limiting prism. Thus no assertion of tangential absolute continuity along zero-face relative interiors follows from the linked-row compactness hypotheses. The vector flux reads -n_0(2sqrt(2))=(0,2,2)=M(0,c,c)(4/c), exactly as required.

## 7. Every finite atomic tangential measure can be realized

Here is a precise larger class, still without a deepestness claim. Fix distinct p_1<...<p_k in (0,1) and desired positive raw inverse defect masses r_i. Choose a positive convex PL H that is affine in a neighborhood of each p_i and has a strictly positive slope jump at one point in every gap (p_i,p_(i+1)). For k=1 a constant H suffices. Put

    delta_j=1/j, eta_j=exp(-j^2),
    w_ij=delta_j r_i/[2H(p_i)],
    E_ij=[p_i-w_ij,p_i+w_ij].

For large j the intervals are disjoint and contained in the affine neighborhoods. Define A_j to equal H on these bands. In each gap between adjacent bands replace H by the chord joining the endpoint values. Convexity of H places that chord above H, and its slope lies between the adjacent slopes of H, so this replacement remains convex. To the left of the first band set A_j=H+dist(s,E_1j), and to the right of the last band use A_j=H+dist(s,E_kj). These exterior choices introduce the correct upward slope jumps. Thus A_j>=H is convex finite-PL, its slopes and values are uniformly bounded, and equality holds exactly on the bands, apart from irrelevant isolated seams.

Use (1) with A_j and the new eta_j. On each band,

    delta_j j^2 integral_(E_ij) H(s)ds=r_i,

exactly, since H is affine and the band is centered at p_i. Off the bands, each chord gap rises at a slope bounded away from zero from its two endpoints, uniformly for large j; there are finitely many gaps. The same integrable |log distance| bound as Section 6 makes their entire contribution vanish. Therefore

    zeta=(2/c) sum_i r_i delta_(p_i,0,0),
    b=sqrt(2) sum_i r_i delta_(n_0,p_i,0,0).           (16)

Choosing r_i equal to a prescribed boundary atom mass divided by sqrt(2) realizes that arbitrary finite atomic boundary measure. The exact rows are again the finitely many active H-cell rows from Section 4. Every cell has a fixed positive ordinary-volume component, so its limiting source remains interior and its marked value stays positive. No vanishing-source-weight loophole or increasing number of parameter planes is used.

The construction does not settle which nonatomic singular measures are realizable with a fixed plane budget, or what the additional actual deepestness and ordinary physical stress may exclude. It gives a concrete counterexample to any lower-dimensional reduction that imports concave-density, convex-support, or tangential absolute-continuity structure solely from the already proved geometry and volume contact rows.

## 8. One affine plane also gives a non-log-concave density with full support

There is a different one-row obstruction without tangential singularity. Fix a closed nontrivial interval I strictly inside [0,1], put D(s)=dist(s,I), and define

    delta_j=1/j,
    K_j={0<=s<=1,x,y>=0:
                   delta_j+exp(-j)D(s)<=x+y<=1},
    ell_j=x+y-delta_j+exp(-2j),
    L_j=c_j ell_j.                                   (17)

The lower roof is convex, and the parameter is affine and strictly positive. Once again K_j tends to the same prism and c_j tends to exp(1/2). On the lower roof the raw parameter equals exp(-j)D(s)+exp(-2j). Its negative logarithm divided by j tends to 2 on I and to 1 at every point outside I. The roof area density multiplied by j tends uniformly to sqrt(2); the lower normals tend uniformly to n_0. The logarithmic weight is bounded above by 2j plus a fixed normalization constant. Dominated convergence therefore proves

    b=sqrt(2)[1+1_I(s)] ds delta_(n_0,s,0,0).         (18)

As before the other facets contribute only the ordinary trace. Decomposing t/(t-delta_j+exp(-2j)) as in Section 2 gives raw inverse defect [1+1_I(s)]ds, so

    zeta=(2/c)[1+1_I(s)] ds delta_(s,0,0).            (19)

There is one exact row proportional to dm_j/ell_j, with original-volume row exactly uniform. For the explicit choice I=[1/3,2/3], the total raw inverse mass tends to 7/3, and symmetry gives

    Y_j -> (1/2,3/28,3/28),
    L_j(Y_j) -> 3c/14.                               (20)

Thus the same one-row uniform source-core and marked-value bounds hold. The density in (18) has full interval support but a genuine interior jump. A positive log-concave density on an interval is continuous in its interior, since its logarithm is a finite concave function there. No a.e. modification removes this jump. Hence (18) is not log-concave, even though a single affine parameter and a single exact contact source suffice.

This example separates two issues: a complicated parameter-cell decomposition is unnecessary for non-log-concave tangential density, and a singular tangential defect is unnecessary for the same failure. The geometric mechanism is the two distinct exponential floor scales in (17), which ordinary Hausdorff and uniform-parameter convergence do not record. As with (12), the marks are not claimed deepest or physically stationary.

The exact companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_disconnected_tangential_defect_profiles_slab_recovery.py` checks the coarea primitive, lower-surface Jacobian, profile incidences, row moments, and the vector/radial flux normalizations. The weak-limit and source-core conclusions are analytic arguments in Sections 2--4.
